target.what: Upper bound of the US federal funds target range after the next FOMC meeting following 2026-10-15
target.publisher: Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
target.cadence: Scheduled FOMC meetings approximately every 6-8 weeks; decision announced at meeting end
target.caveats: The next FOMC meeting after 2026-10-15 is not explicitly known from the cutoff. The FOMC typically meets 8 times per year; the next meeting after mid-October 2026 is likely in early November or December 2026. The target is the upper bound of the target range for the federal funds rate, set by the FO

candidates.perspective: FOMC historical decisions and current target range
candidates.hypothesis: The current upper bound as of 2026-10-15 and recent FOMC decisions provide the baseline for the next meeting. The next decision is likely a continuation or a small adjustment from the current level.
candidates.data_to_find: FOMC meeting calendar for 2026, especially the meeting dates after 2026-10-15; the target range upper bound as of the most recent meeting before 2026-10-15; the statement and vote from that meeting.

methods.rationale: The current upper bound is 4.00% (p3/p8/p39/p50), so the only plausible outcomes at the next meeting are a hold at 4.00%, a 25bp hike to 4.25%, or a 25bp cut to 3.75%. No market-implied probabilities for the specific next meeting are available in the kept evidence, so the hike and cut probabilities are declared as assumptions (a1, a2) anchored on the historical base rate of changes (p57/p60) and the hot September CPI (p20/p21). The remainder is assigned to 4.50% rather than 4.00% because the schema requires a single remainder outcome and the hold is the modal outcome; this is a known limitation of the method and the reason a market-implied probability input (b1) is the top follow-up. Shared dependency: all inputs rest on the September 2026 level and the assumption that the next meeting is a normal scheduled meeting.

assumptions.name: Probability of a 25bp hike to 4.25% at the next meeting
assumptions.rationale: September CPI came in hot (3.7% headline, 0.6% m/m, above consensus) and the Fed had just hiked 25bp in September, so a follow-up hike is plausible; but the longer-run SEP midpoint of 3.1% (p68) implies the current 4.00% upper bound is already restrictive, and the historical base rate of a change at any given decision is only about 35% (p57/p60), so a hike is not the baseline.
assumptions.applies_when: The next FOMC meeting after 2026-10-15 is a scheduled meeting and no major financial-stability shock intervenes.
assumptions.falsified_by: Market-implied odds for a hike at the next meeting falling below 10% or rising above 45%, or a Fed communication explicitly ruling out further tightening.

assumptions.name: Probability of a 25bp cut to 3.75% at the next meeting
assumptions.rationale: With inflation at 3.7% and the Fed having just hiked, an immediate reversal to a cut is unlikely; the historical base rate of cuts is 58/316 ≈ 18% per decision (p59/p54), but the current hawkish stance and hot CPI argue for a much lower near-term cut probability.
assumptions.applies_when: No sharp deterioration in the labour market or financial conditions before the next meeting.
assumptions.falsified_by: A weak October employment report or a market-implied cut probability above 15%.

methods.rationale: Uses the most direct market-implied probabilities for the next FOMC meeting from CME FedWatch as of 2026-10-14: p93 gives 56.3% for a hold at 4.00% and p92 gives 43.7% for a 25bp hike to 4.25%. The 4.75%, 5.00%, 5.25% and 5.50%-or-higher labels are folded into the 4.50% remainder because the market snapshot prices no such moves and the Fed has not signalled a larger step. Shared dependency: p92 and p93 come from the same CME FedWatch snapshot and are complementary, so they are not independent. Failure mode: if the next meeting is not the one priced by the 2026-10-14 snapshot (e.g., the next meeting is in December 2026), these probabilities are for the wrong meeting.
